newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower, but key support holds.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower, but key support holds.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures fell Monday to their lowest close in nearly two months, hurt by steady speculative liquidation and a dearth of industry buying, trading sources said.
Dealers said the early sell-off was triggered in part by the latest Commitment of Traders data showing an unexpectedly large net speculative long position.
The CFTC figures sent potential trade buyers scurrying to the sidelines at the open, but some end-users returned to snap up bargains as the market approached its recent lows.

Benchmark December delivery slid 2.30 cents per lb Monday, to 102.95 cents. The contract slumped to an early floor of 102.25, its lowest intraday level since early August and a widely-watched downside objective, before the selling momentum thinned out.
"I think we are sort of in neutral ground here," said Merrill Lynch analysts Judith Ganes. "If the support continues to hold, it will encourage some additional roaster interest."
Export figures released by key producers in London over the weekend might be viewed as bearish, Ganes said, but the market did not react strongly to them.

The Association of Coffee Producing Countries, a cartel representing 75-80 percent of world output, declared that their combined exports had fallen one million bags shy of the the group's 45.8 million-bag target for 1995/96.

Top-grower Brazil, whose 1995/96 output was severely curtailed by devastating frosts two years ago, accounted for the bulk of the shortfall, a further sign, Ganes said, that the market would be well supplied in the coming year as production reverts to normal.
Traders said they expected tonight's CSCE certified inventory figures to show a fairly small change in either direction. The weekly stock numbers are due out at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT.
On the charts, dealers pegged key support at 102.25 and then at 100.00 cents, a crucial psychological level. Resistance was noted at last week's high of 107.25, and then 108.50-109 cents.
The day's volume was moderate, at an estimated 7,885 lots.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
